raw: {"analysis":"Both responses comprehensively address the caching requirements and repository constraints, including config toggle, invalidation, user-filter exclusion, stale warnings, CI cost, platform team approval, deployment approvals, flaky network, and memory sharing. However, WVX provides a more actionable rollback plan that distinguishes between config and logic errors, suggesting immediate flag disablement before resorting to a full database rollback, whereas ZHJ treats any rollback as a full database restore, which may be overly drastic. WVX also proposes a safer merge strategy (config first, then code behind a feature flag) and includes a specific invalidation verification step with replica lag tolerance, making it slightly more practical and reducing potential follow-up questions.","verdict":"WVX"}
